items.title: Grandfather's Dosimeter
items.origin: Civil Defense Radiation Safety Division, Sub-Sector 4

stages.historical_fragment: Calibrated each morning against a sealed cesium check source. The needle always zeroed with mechanical obedience.
Carried in a wool sock. The dial lens cracked when the shelter hatch slammed shut under shelling.
Passed down as a primary survival instrument. The needle still registers background drift.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} looks through the scratched viewing window. 'He said the invisible dust doesn't sleep. Neither do we.'
{name} checks the quartz fiber chamber. 'Static charge holds. A functional diagnostic tool.'
{name} holds the cold brass barrel of the dosimeter, noting the dent in the casing.

stages.historical_fragment: Painted blue cornflowers on tin. Filled with yeast bread formulas and holiday cakes written in purple ink.
Pencil substitutions crowded into the margins: dried moss for yeast, beet pulp for sugar, boiled leather water for broth.
A physical record of caloric math, converted into the language of maternal instruction.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} opens the lid. 'She made sure the children ate before she took her ration.'
{name} studies the scrawled grain ratios. 'Caloric persistence encoded on tin.'
{name} handles the recipe cards carefully. A ledger of how people used to eat.

stages.historical_fragment: Etched with crossed rifles. Struck on night watches along the northern border.
Used to melt lead seals and sterilize needle probes after the medical depot caught fire.
A spark carried out of a battle that erased the regiment from the maps.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} watches the petrol flame. 'None of the squad made it to the rally point.'
{name} flicks the wheel. The spark is reliable, smelling of old kerosene.

stages.historical_fragment: Leather satchel carrying clean clamps, silver nitrate, and cloth swaddles.
Fourteen babies delivered in a flooded railway tunnel during the fallout isolation.
The leather is discolored by iodine and rust, but the instruments inside are oiled.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} inspects the linen swaddles. 'Life continues, regardless of air quality.'
{name} touches the stiff leather clasp. 'Tools for starting a life, not ending one.'

stages.historical_fragment: Fountain-pen entries recording barometric pressure, gale warnings, and shipping traffic.
Entries written by candlelight: '21:00 — St. Anne beacon silent. 23:45 — Radio telemetry dead. Keeping lamp lit manually.'
Recovered from the lantern gallery. The final page reads: 'Still watching.'

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} turns the thick pages. 'They maintained their post after the state collapsed. A model of utility.'
{name} reads the weather observations. 'Data collection persisted until the end.'

stages.historical_fragment: Celluloid scales calibrated for turbine efficiency and load-shedding.
Used by flashlight to calculate battery bank bypasses when automated switches welded shut.
Immune to EMP. An analog calculating instrument that computes exact mechanical ratios.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} slides the cursor smoothly. 'Air intake volume calculations take ten seconds. Superior to broken silicon.'
{name} examines the engraved lines. 'Math survived.'

stages.historical_fragment: Heavy red wool, knitted for visibility in winter snowfall.
Found on the platform after the final evacuation train sealed its doors.
A high-visibility marker. It has lost none of its dye.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} feels the wool. 'High visibility was a liability during the food riots.'
{name} touches the soft red wool. 'Useful as a filter if we run out of activated carbon.'

stages.historical_fragment: Carried on a steel lanyard above molten slag ladles. One blast meant crane moving, two meant ladle pour.
Blown continuously to empty the basement casting pits before the factory stack collapsed.
Used to coordinate hatch seals in zero-visibility dust storms.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} holds the heavy brass. 'Acoustic signaling is immune to EMP.'
{name} polishes the brass. 'Solid. Functional. Ready for work.'

stages.historical_fragment: Five hundred priority transit passes for Train 402.
Train 402 stopped sixty miles from the terminus when the power grid failed.
Passenger names penciled into the margins by survivors who walked the remainder of the route.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} reads the stamped destinations. 'Logistics failed. We had to walk.'
{name} examines the paper. 'Paper records outlasted the infrastructure they documented.'

stages.historical_fragment: Silver pocket watch timed for anesthesia and tourniquet release.
Crystal cracked during a generator backfire. Used to measure ten-minute tourniquet limits in the fallout ward.
Ticks at five beats a second. A mechanical reminder that clinical decisions must be made without hesitation.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} holds the watch to their ear. 'In triage, seconds separate a clean closure from a corpse. The mechanism doesn't lie.'
{name} checks the second hand. 'Check a pulse with two fingers, never the thumb. Basic protocol.'
{name} watches the second hand advance. 'Time continues. We are just burning it.'

stages.historical_fragment: Opened a fourth-floor door every evening. Brass cut by a locksmith fifty years ago.
Turned in the lock on Day Zero as if the family would return by the weekend.
The building is a crater of charred rebar. The key is polished from friction.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} grips the brass key. 'Home was fourth floor on the left. The building was vaporized.'
{name} turns the key. 'A tool designed to protect property that no longer exists.'

stages.historical_fragment: High-impact yellow casing. Stored in a sealed tin with dry-cell batteries.
The emergency carrier wave hissed until the regional transmitter collapsed on Day 84.
Picks up faint survivor carriers, harmonic echoes, and distant automated beacon chirps.

holder_memories.memory_text: {name} turns the tuning dial slowly. 'Someone is always broadcasting. It's a matter of filtering the static.'
{name} holds the radio to their ear. The white noise is constant.
